result.summary: The street provides basic pedestrian infrastructure with continuous sidewalks on both sides, though they lack a buffer from traffic. Safety is compromised by faded crosswalk markings and significant visual obstructions from parked cars near the intersection.

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The transverse crosswalk markings at the intersection are heavily worn, making the pedestrian crossing area less visible to approaching motorists.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground intersection area across the main roadway

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions from Parking
hazards.description: Parked vehicles are situated very close to the intersection, blocking sightlines between pedestrians attempting to cross and oncoming drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curbs on both sides of the street leading up to the intersection

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Replace faded transverse lines with high-visibility continental or ladder-style markings to increase driver awareness of the crossing.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at the intersection to shorten the crossing distance, improve pedestrian visibility, and prevent illegal parking near the corner.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to ensure clear sightlines for all road users.

result.summary: The image depicts a typical urban residential street with row houses and parallel parking on both sides. While sidewalks are present, they are narrow and obstructed by utility poles, and the continuous line of parked vehicles creates significant visual barriers between the walkway and the roadway.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Utility poles are located directly in the center of the narrow sidewalk, significantly reducing the effective clear width for pedestrians and those with mobility aids.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image on the sidewalk

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: A continuous line of parked cars, including large SUVs, blocks sightlines between pedestrians on the sidewalk and drivers in the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curb line on both sides of the street

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) at potential crossing points to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces near utility poles or potential crossing points to improve sightlines and provide more space for pedestrian movement.

interventions.title: Street Trees
interventions.description: Incorporate street trees to provide a vertical buffer between the sidewalk and the road, while also providing shade and improving the aesthetic environment.

result.summary: The street features a two-lane roadway with parallel parking and sidewalks on both sides, though the right-side walkway is in poor condition. There is a complete absence of marked crossings, traffic calming, or pedestrian-scale lighting, and parked vehicles create significant sightline obstructions.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Continuous parallel parking on both sides of the street obscures pedestrians from the view of approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both curbs throughout the midground

hazards.name: Sidewalk Discontinuity
hazards.description: The sidewalk on the right side transitions into an unpaved or severely degraded surface, creating a tripping hazard.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the street in the foreground and midground

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at the ends of the block to improve visibility between pedestrians and motorists and shorten crossing distances.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install zebra-style marked crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way at crossing points.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Rehabilitation
interventions.description: Repair and pave the sidewalk on the right side to provide a continuous, accessible walking surface.

result.summary: The street features a continuous, wide concrete sidewalk with a clear curb separation from the roadway. However, a large curb cut creates a significant conflict zone, and there is a lack of vertical buffers like trees or bollards between pedestrians and traffic.

hazards.name: Wide Driveway/Curb Cut
hazards.description: A wide concrete apron across the sidewalk increases the area where vehicles may cross the pedestrian path, creating conflict points.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: No physical separation like trees, bollards, or parked cars exists between the sidewalk and the travel lane.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Planters
interventions.description: Install street trees or large planters to provide a physical and psychological buffer between pedestrians and the roadway.

interventions.title: Driveway Narrowing
interventions.description: Reduce the width of the curb cut to the minimum necessary for vehicle access to minimize the pedestrian-vehicle conflict zone.
